claims.name: lambda(p) is EVEN for every row pair of all three icosahedral machines (a line separates with both its columns or with neither), and for M_edge the hardest pair has lambda = 12 = 6 lines x 2

TIE MECHANISM LEMMA (verified on every (pair, line) of all three machines): for the two columns u, -u of one line, (a) if u is perpendicular to exactly one member of the pair then EXACTLY ONE of the two columns separates it (tau gives the same value to both tie entries); (b) otherwise the two columns agree. This explains why lambda need not be 2 x (number of lines)

CORRECTION (original FAIL kept as registered, no relaxation): lambda_min(M_edge) = 12 columns but they span 11 LINES, not 6 -- the "even = 2 per line" reading is refuted by the tie mechanism lemma (P2a-3): tie lines contribute a single separating column. The value lambda_min = 12 (R6) stands; only its line decomposition changes

EXPLORATORY (found this round, not pre-registered): the CROSS complement law lambda(r, -r`) + lambda(r, r`) = N holds for every row pair of every icosahedral machine that has no column perpendicular to both rows -- each column splits between the pair and its cross image, so their separating sets are complementary (sum = N). Note the ANTIPODAL image pair (r, r`) -> (-r, -r`) instead keeps lambda unchanged

claims.name: BLIND PREDICTION: lambda decreases monotonically as the pair gets closer (|dot| larger), and the 6 separating lines of the hardest pair are ALL E-type (2-fold axes)

CORRECTION (same run, no relaxation of the original): (i) lambda is NOT a function of |dot| -- each shell splits into TWO orbits whose lambdas are complementary (sum = N), so the notion of a single "hardest shell" is wrong; the correct statement is that the global minimum lambda = 12 is attained on the 36-degree shell; (ii) the 6 separating lines are NOT all E-type but a mix of V/F/E

claims.name: exact algebraic characterisation verified for every (pair, column) of all three machines: <u,r><u,r`> = (<u,r+r`>^2 - <u,r-r`>^2)/4 and u separates the pair  <=>  <u,r+r`>^2 < <u,r-r`>^2, i.e. u points closer to the DIFFERENCE direction than to the SUM (bisector) direction (tie entries, where the dot is exactly 0, are excluded: they are resolved by the frozen tau rule, not by the dot)
